title: The garment approaches a passport
technology: EU identifiers, data carriers, registry, APIs and textile product data
governingQuestion: How will product evidence move from a brand file into interoperable public infrastructure?
status: evidence-backed production draft; recording, interviews, specialist review and owner-final approval remain open

longform.headline: The garment approaches a passport
longform.opening: A garment passport is becoming operational EU infrastructure—not a Fashion Week prop.

sections.heading: Then
sections.copy: The EU adopted ESPR in 2024, establishing a framework that includes Digital Product Passports; the Commission identifies textile apparel as a priority product group.

sections.heading: Now
sections.copy: The Commission says the DPP Registry launched in July 2026 with user-interface and API registration, access management, logging and machine-readable vocabulary support.

sections.heading: Next—and the limit
sections.copy: The presence of EU infrastructure does not prove that every CPHFW garment already carries a textile DPP or that one event-level product-data stack has been selected.

longform.closing: Copenhagen’s distinction is not a claim of purity. It is the decision to make participation depend on evidence—and the obligation to keep asking what that evidence cannot establish.

spokenScript: A garment passport is becoming operational EU infrastructure—not a Fashion Week prop.
The EU adopted ESPR in 2024, establishing a framework that includes Digital Product Passports; the Commission identifies textile apparel as a priority product group.
The Commission says the DPP Registry launched in July 2026 with user-interface and API registration, access management, logging and machine-readable vocabulary support.
The system: EU identifiers, data carriers, registry, APIs and textile product data.
The record: EU Digital Product Passport Registry.
The boundary: The presence of EU infrastructure does not prove that every CPHFW garment already carries a textile DPP or that one event-level product-data stack has been selected.
